The Goodman-Bacon decomposition of a two-way fixed-effects estimate

Source: R/policy_evaluation.R
bacondcmp.Rd

Splits the two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences estimate of a staggered adoption into the two-group, two-period comparisons it averages, with their weights: treated against never treated, earlier against later treated, and later against earlier treated (the comparisons that use already-treated units as controls).

Usage

bacondcmp(data, unit, time, y, trtd)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

trtd

Column name of the treatment indicator (0 or 1).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_bacon: type ("treated vs never", "earlier vs later", "later vs earlier"), treated, control (the adoption periods; Inf for never), estimate, weight; attribute twfe (the weighted sum, equal to the two-way estimate).

Details

For a balanced panel with treatment that stays on and no covariates, the estimate of plndid is exactly \(\hat\beta = \sum_{k} s_{kU}\hat\beta_{kU} + \sum_{k \ne l} s_{kl}\hat\beta_{kl}\), with weights that sum to one and grow with the groups' sizes \(n\) and the variance of their treatment over time \(\bar D(1 - \bar D)\) (Goodman-Bacon 2021, theorem 1). Units treated from the first period act as an already-treated group. A large weight on "later vs earlier" comparisons, together with effects that grow over time, is the warning sign that the two-way estimate is biased.

References

Goodman-Bacon A (2021). Difference-in-differences with variation in treatment timing. Journal of Econometrics 225(2):254-277. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.03.014

See also

plndid, stgatt.

Examples

p <- polex()
b <- bacondcmp(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "reformed")
b
#> Goodman-Bacon decomposition: two-way estimate -3.232
#>   earlier vs later   weight 0.209, average estimate -3.558
#>   later vs earlier   weight 0.209, average estimate -3.414
#>   treated vs never   weight 0.581, average estimate -3.048
tapply(b$weight, b$type, sum)
#> earlier vs later later vs earlier treated vs never 
#>        0.2093023        0.2093023        0.5813953
